approved: Personal Property Securities Amendment (Deregulatory Measures) Bill 2014

Introduced the Personal Property Securities Amendment (Deregulatory Measures) Bill 2014 to ease compliance burdens on the hire and rental industry, which turns over around $6.6 billion and employs over 18,000 Australians, and said clarifying the definition of a motor vehicle and removing a lease-registration requirement would save business over $11 million a year.

The speaker supported the Personal Property Securities Amendment (Deregulatory Measures) Bill 2014, which abolishes the 90-day rule for leases of serial numbered goods like motor vehicles, simplifying the PPSA scheme.

The speaker supported the Personal Property Securities Amendment (Deregulatory Measures) Bill 2014, arguing it would repeal the 90-day registration rule for serial-numbered goods leased by hire companies, saving businesses like R&R Hire thousands of dollars and enabling them to hire new staff. He also highlighted the government's broader deregulation agenda, which exceeded a $1 billion annual red-tape reduction target.

The speaker supported the Personal Property Securities Amendment (Deregulatory Measures) Bill 2014, describing it as a small reform that builds on the 2009 consolidation of over 70 pieces of legislation into a single personal property securities system and will help small businesses.

The speaker argued that the Personal Property Securities Amendment (Deregulatory Measures) Bill 2014 would reduce the administrative burden on small businesses, citing 21,000 additional regulations and 519,000 job losses under the previous Labor government, and noted the bill would save the rental industry $11 million annually. The speaker also announced a statutory review of the Personal Property Securities Act.

The speaker argued that the Personal Property Securities Amendment (Deregulatory Measures) Bill 2014 simplifies the PPS regime by changing the lease term threshold for serial-numbered goods from 90 days to 12 months, and announced Labor’s support for the bill.

The bill amends the Personal Property Securities Act to remove the requirement to register leases of 90 days to less than 12 months, saving an estimated $11.2 million in costs for businesses and customers.

The Personal Property Securities Amendment (Deregulatory Measures) Bill 2014 was argued to simplify the Personal Property Securities Act, reduce costs and confusion for business, especially small equipment-hire firms, following consultation with the hire industry. The statutory review of the act, led by Bruce Whittaker, has been completed and is under government consideration.
